chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: First recordings, Irving Mills and Will Hudson's arrangements
summary: Crawford says the band first recorded in New York, was tied to Irving Mills's office, and he disliked Will Hudson's charts.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you all recording -- you all were recording now, right?
Yeah, records were coming out of those.
And you -- do you remember the first recording that you made with the band?
No. I remember that junk like drum (inaudible) Will Hudson used to write, because he was working out at Mills' office, Irving Mills' office.
This was after you got to New York.
Yeah. That's, you know, Duke -- Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington were working out of his office, Irving Mills.
Yeah, he lives in Hollywood or Beverly Hills, I think, now.
That was another one.
You didn't like him too much?
No, because he was -- he made Will Hudson our arranger, and he came out -- started writing that old White Heat stuff and all that, which I can't stomach, things like that.
Well now, how did you all -- how did you all -- did you all get the job with the Lafayette through Irving Mills or did you get -- did you all become --
I really don't know.
-- did you all become involved with Mills after you got to New York?
Maybe Oxley got us that job. I don't know. I don't know how we got it because we were recording, and that perhaps [loosened] us.
So you'd been recording -- you'd been recording -- had you -- had you been recording, did you do records when you were in Cleveland and Cincinnati with the band?
No.
You didn't start recording with the band --
Until New York.
-- until you got to New York.
Yeah.
Okay. And then --
